name: Smart Contracts and Executable Terms
title: Smart Contracts and Executable Terms
answer: Smart contracts and executable terms cover agreements whose performance is carried out by code rather than by a person reading a clause and acting on it. The scope runs from simple on chain transfers that release payment when a condition is met, to hybrid arrangements where a conventional written contract governs the deal and a program handles settlement, escrow or milestone release. It also takes in the drafting question of how natural language terms and code are meant to line up when the two disagree. Most work in this area sits at the seam between the legal document and the software that enforces part of it.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Smart contracts and executable terms cover agreements whose performance is carried out by code rather than by a person reading a clause and acting on it. The scope runs from simple on chain transfers that release payment when a condition is met, to hybrid arrangements where a conventional written contract governs the deal and a program handles settlement, escrow or milestone release. It also takes in the drafting question of how natural language terms and code are meant to line up when the two disagree. Most work in this area sits at the seam between the legal document and the software that enforces part of it.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: Execution depends on a deterministic environment, most often a blockchain such as Ethereum, where a deployed program runs the same way on every node and its results are recorded on a public ledger. Oracles feed outside facts, prices or delivery confirmations into that environment, since a chain cannot see the world on its own. Off chain, teams use version control, test networks and audit tooling before anything is deployed, and the contract text itself usually lives in an ordinary document store alongside the code. Wallets and keys are the practical interface: whoever holds the signing key can trigger the terms.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The work starts by reducing an agreement to conditions that a machine can evaluate: what must be true, what gets transferred, and in what order. Drafters write the prose, developers write the program, and the two are reconciled line by line so that each obligation has a counterpart in code or is explicitly left to human performance. Testing happens on simulated networks with edge cases, failed transfers and disputed inputs, and independent review checks for logic errors before deployment. Because a deployed program is difficult to change, the review stage carries more weight than it would for ordinary software.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: The central risk is that code executes exactly as written, including when it was written wrong, so errors, exploits and unintended transfers are hard to reverse. Allocation of liability between the drafter, the developer and the operator is often unclear, and courts have only begun to treat these arrangements, with this site tracking 29 AI case law precedents and 152 active AI lawsuits across the field. Provenance matters too: which version of the code ran, what inputs it received, and whether the written contract was amended after deployment. Record keeping, audit trails and clear statements of which document controls in a conflict are the usual controls.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Expect more standard form templates and clause libraries that pair prose with reference implementations, so drafting and deployment stop being separate exercises. Regulated sectors will push for identity, permissioning and reporting built into the execution layer rather than bolted on. Dispute resolution is likely to move toward agreed expert determination and arbitration for code related failures, since litigation over a deterministic transfer is slow and expensive. The open question is whether executable terms remain a settlement mechanism attached to a contract, or become the contract itself.
